AF's fix is real and correct for the case it names.
measured_zero_provider_calls.this_draws_finding_takes_a_different_gat: This draw's F06 has fact_ids: [] (the LLM sample did not self-cite the fact this time, though it is the same substantive complaint), so cited_fact_defect falls to its 'reviewed unit's own citations' branch (item 83/91's unit_fact_ids), which requires _reviewed_unit_fact_ids(quote, units) to locate the one content unit whose OWN text carries the quote.
measured_zero_provider_calls.the_lookup_fails_structurally: content_units.json's documentation_resources unit for link_target:023 carries fact_ids ['link_target:023'] and text 'The Code of Conduct outlines expected behavior for participants contributing to or engaging with the Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java community.' - the descriptive sentence ALONE. The renderer composes the visible bullet as its own chrome prefix ('- **[Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)** — ') followed by that unit's text. The reviewer's quote is the FULL rendered line, chrome included. quote_located(quote, unit_text) returns False: the normalized whole-quote containment check fails because the unit's text lacks the renderer's prefix entirely, and the 80-character opening-anchor check (_ANCHOR_LENGTH) also fails because it anchors the match to the quote's own OPENING characters - which are exactly the renderer's prefix, absent from the haystack. Confirmed directly: _reviewed_unit_fact_ids(quote, units) returns () for this quote against this content_units.json, and cited_fact_defect(finding, quote, by_id, ()) therefore returns None even though link_target:023 (SUPPORTED, value CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) is plainly the unit's own citation and the quote plainly carries its value inside link syntax.

blocking_finding_F06.root_cause: quote_located's existing anchor rule (docs: 'a long quote anchors by its opening... a reviewer that copies a whole block and drifts in its tail still points at real text') only tolerates drift AFTER the matched prefix. It has no rule for a quote whose EXTRA text is a renderer-added PREFIX ahead of the unit's own sentence - the inverse drift shape, produced whenever a documentation_resources (or any bullet-styled) unit's rendered line is chrome-prefix + unit-text-suffix and a reviewer quotes the whole rendered line.
blocking_finding_F06.fix_proposed: Widen _carried_by_units / _reviewed_unit_fact_ids (never quote_located's general contract, which absence_defect and review_checks also rely on) so that, when the whole-quote and opening-anchor checks both fail, a unit is still 'carrying' the quote if the unit's own normalized text is itself a sufficiently long (>= _ANCHOR_LENGTH, or the whole of a short unit's own text) trailing substring of the quote's normalized form - a closing anchor, symmetric to the existing opening one, scoped narrowly to the unit-lookup helpers rather than to quote_located's own general documented contract.
blocking_finding_F06.alternative_rejected: Widening quote_located itself: absence_defect and review_checks both call quote_located directly for a different question (does the candidate/section contain this text at all), where a bare closing-anchor match on a short claim string risks false positives quote_located's own length floors were written to avoid; the two callers that actually need this (_carried_by_units, _reviewed_unit_fact_ids) already apply their own length-gated fragment logic beside it, so the fix belongs there.
blocking_finding_F06.mutation_test: A finding quoting a bullet's full rendered line (renderer chrome-prefix + a unit's own trailing sentence) whose value a cited-or-reviewed-unit fact backs must fold via cited_fact_defect; an otherwise-identical quote whose trailing sentence no unit wrote must still stand.
blocking_finding_F06.not_this_lanes_to_write: review/ is shared code; lane-c never patches it. Recorded as a PROPOSAL for the owner/reviewer to route.
